prose:
John Gruber reacts to Reuters' reporting on Anthropic's IPO prospectus. Reuters says the filing frames AI as a bet on transforming the economy more than industrialization, electricity or the internet. Gruber argues that framing undersells it: the IPO only makes sense if Anthropic itself, not AI in general, is about to win the race to a super-intelligence.

He points to the numbers as the other half of the story: a reported $42 billion net loss in 2025 and $518 billion of planned cloud and infrastructure commitments. He is openly skeptical of any claim that the company is profitable, expecting leaks built on undefined accounting. (Based on the excerpt in the feed item; the Reuters article itself was not retrieved.)
highlights: Gruber reads the prospectus as a bet that Anthropic alone, not AI broadly, will win
$518B of planned compute and infrastructure obligations
Commentary on Reuters reporting, not the filing itself
